chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: I was told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ibrahim bin Hashim, from Ubaidullah bin Musa al-‘Absi, from Sa’d bin Turayf, from Abu Ja’far (peace be upon him), that he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said:
O Ali, when the Day of Resurrection shall be, I, you and Jibra’eel will sit upon the Path, and none will pass except for those who have a book that includes the acquittal of your befriendship.

key_terms.الصِّرَاط: The Path (Sirat, the bridge over Hell)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for passing the Sirat according to this hadith from Abu Ja'far?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* underscores the centrality of Ali ibn Abi Talib’s wilayah as the decisive criterion for salvation on the Day of Resurrection. It highlights a unique eschatological role where the Prophet, Ali, and Jibra’il jointly oversee the crossing of the Sirat, linking spiritual authority directly to divine judgment. This narrative reinforces the Shia belief that allegiance to the Ahl al-Bayt is not merely a historical loyalty but a metaphysical prerequisite for entering Paradise.

en.basel-kadem: 6.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: I was told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ibrahim bin Hashim, from Ubaidullah bin Musa al-‘Absi, from Sa’d bin Turayf, from Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him, that he said: The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family:
O Ali, when the Day of Resurrection shall be, I, you and Jibra’eel will sit upon the Path, and none will pass except for those who have a book that includes the acquittal of your befriendship.
